novel_features.name: Live triage pulse
novel_features.description: One offline call shows what's hot right now: open incidents bucketed by service, urgency and status with how long each has gone unacknowledged, sorted by SLA risk.

novel_features.name: On-call now + next + handoff
novel_features.description: Resolves who is on call right now for a service or team, who is on next, and the exact handoff timestamp.

novel_features.name: Escalation coverage audit
novel_features.description: Flags services whose escalation chain is broken: empty tiers, single point of failure, expired or empty schedules, or no escalation policy at all.

novel_features.name: MTTA / MTTR analytics
novel_features.description: Mean time to acknowledge and resolve, computed from synced log-entry timestamps and grouped by service, team or priority.

novel_features.name: On-call hours report
novel_features.description: On-call hours per user over a time window, derived from synced schedule layers and overrides.

novel_features.name: Responder workload + off-hours
novel_features.description: Per-responder page, ack and resolve counts plus the share of pages that landed off-hours (nights and weekends).

novel_features.name: Noisy-service ranking
novel_features.description: Ranks services by incident volume, auto-resolve rate and re-trigger/flapping rate over a window.

novel_features.name: Incident timeline
novel_features.description: Reconstructs one incident's full chronology — trigger, every ack, note, reassignment, escalation and resolve — with elapsed deltas between events.

novel_features.name: Change-event correlation
novel_features.description: For an incident, see the change events that shipped on the same service in the window right before it triggered, ranked by proximity.

novel_features.name: Schedule gap audit
novel_features.description: Find future time windows where a schedule has nobody on call, before an incident finds the hole for you.

novel_features.name: Stale incident sweep
novel_features.description: Open incidents with no log activity past a threshold, grouped by responder and service — the ones quietly rotting.
